title: Evaluating AI-Driven Speech Recognition Tools for Pronunciation Training Among EFL Learners
content: Artificial intelligence driven speech recognition is increasingly used to support pronunciation practice in English as a Foreign Language (EFL) learning, yet less attention has been given to how learners experience and interpret automated feedback during actual learning activities. This study examined EFL learners’ experiences with AI driven speech recognition for pronunciation training, focusing on feedback usefulness, recognition limitations, changes in learning strategies, and teacher mediation. A qualitative interpretive design was employed with undergraduate EFL learners who engaged in pronunciation activities supported by an AI driven speech recognition tool. Data were collected through semi structured interviews, classroom observations, learner reflection logs, and digital learning artifacts and analyzed using reflexive thematic analysis. The findings showed that learners valued immediate feedback because it enabled repeated practice, self monitoring, and independent correction. However, recognition inconsistencies sometimes made it difficult to determine whether unsuccessful evaluations reflected pronunciation problems or system limitations. Learners therefore interpreted automated feedback critically rather than accepting it as an unquestionable judgment. The findings further indicated that AI supported learner agency, while teacher mediation remained important for clarifying ambiguous feedback and guiding pronunciation adjustments. The study concludes that AI driven speech recognition is most useful as a complementary resource within teacher supported pronunciation instruction, with its pedagogical value depending on both recognition capability and learners’ ability to interpret and use feedback strategically.
